interpretations: Every linewidth is the canonical Gamma = Im Sigma = 1/(2 tau) in angular units, on a finite Brillouin-zone mesh Q of N_q points with branch set iota and basis atoms B. The catalog's composite mode index 3(b-1) + alpha is the pair (b, alpha) of basis atom and Cartesian axis.

compute_isotope_scattering reads frequencies omega, eigenvector components e(q, nu, b, alpha), per-atom mass-variance factors g_b >= 0 and a smearing kernel delta for the energy delta function. The Brillouin-zone sum carries 1/N_q.

compute_linewidth[channel=anharmonic_3ph] reads the kernel |V_3|^2(q nu, q' nu', q - q' nu'') >= 0 as an opaque function, the frequencies, the Bose-Einstein occupation n = 1/(exp(hbar omega/(k_B T)) - 1) and a smearing kernel delta. The third mode is q'' = q - q', so the mesh is a Gamma-centred grid closed under q - q'. The opaque kernel drops the Maradudin-Fein structure, so its exchange symmetry under (q' nu') <-> (q - q' nu'') is a stated hypothesis of the main theorem, not a property of the transcription.
The branch set iota is any finite type and is not tied to three branches per basis atom.
compute_boundary_scattering is the Casimir linewidth |v|/(2L) of a mode with group velocity v and boundary length L > 0. The Casimir rate 1/tau = |v|/L is twice it.
sum_linewidths is Matthiessen's rule Gamma_total = Gamma_anh + Gamma_iso + Gamma_bnd, and solve_bte[bte_solver=rta] is the relaxation-time mean free displacement F = v/(2 Gamma_total).
